label: Matador
body_html: ["div", ["p", "Will Toledo isn't old, but he's feeling his age. He's in debt; his friends are getting married; his hands are frozen; he's stuck in the city; and worst of all, his songs are starting to sound the same. The world is moving past him, blurring into formlessness, and his music as Car Seat Headrest is an attempt to slow down and make sense of the rush."], ["p", ["em", "Teens of Style"], " is technically a compilation, comprising songs dating back to 2011 that were re-recorded for his Matador debut. (", ["em", "Teens of Denial"], ", a planned 2016 release, will be his first Matador album of entirely new material.) You can hear the revised sound as a composite of the label's history: ", ["a", {"href": "https://pitchfork.com/artists/1798-guided-by-voices/", "isExternal": false}, "Guided by Voices"], "' ear for cracked pop oddities, ", ["a", {"href": "https://pitchfork.com/artists/324-belle-and-sebastian/", "isExternal": false}, "Belle and Sebastian"], "'s emotional directness, ", ["a", {"href": "https://pitchfork.com/artists/4699-yo-la-tengo/", "isExternal": false}, "Yo La Tengo"], "'s intimate approach to jamming, ", ["a", {"href": "https://pitchfork.com/artists/26519-stephen-malkmus-and-the-jicks/", "isExternal": false}, "Stephen Malkmus"], "' ability to get wordy without forgetting to rock out. As a songwriter, Toledo is both present and detached, capable of living in a moment while floating above it. A self-summarization comes on the brawny \"Strangers\", when he deadpans a series of autobiographical quips: \"Car seat is a menace to the public,\" \"Car seat is a genetic stop sign,\" \"Car seat's nervous and the lights are bright.\""], ["cm-unit"], ["p", "On that song, we find out the young Toledo fell in love with Michael Stipe: \"I took lyrics out of context and thought, 'he must be speaking to me.'\" His confusion over purposefully abstract lyrics may have turned him into a literalist, someone endeavoring to explain every twist and turn of his interior state. His lyrics are rapaciously intelligent, with a knack for wry humor. Take a lyrical adjustment on the new recordings, for example, that reflects the shift in his life status: \"Times to Die\" swaps a couplet about sneaking his way to musical success into a meditation on the existence of a higher power, like God or (even better) Matador founder Chris Lombardi (\"Got to have faith in the one above me/ Got to believe that Lombardi loves me\"), who will help decide whether or not Toledo is destined to be a cult hero."], ["native-ad", {"position": "in-content", "shouldDisplayLabel": true}], ["p", ["em", "Teens of Style"], " has a noticeably jagged quality; unbelievably, it used to sound even DIY-ier. (The original versions can be found on Car Seat's ", ["a", {"href": "https://carseatheadrest.bandcamp.com/", "rel": "nofollow noopener", "attributes": {"data-offer-url": "https://carseatheadrest.bandcamp.com/"}, "isExternal": true}, "Bandcamp"], ".) The new recordings retain their rough edge, but there's luminescence in the production\u2014the percussion is crisper, the guitars are brighter, and Toledo's singing is a lot more pronounced. The effect is an album that's bookish, but not sedentary. He sells abstruse metaphors and lyrical concepts with every ounce of himself, like failing to do so would mean the end of the world. In this way, he's a cousin of artists like ", ["a", {"href": "https://pitchfork.com/artists/3096-joanna-newsom/", "isExternal": false}, "Joanna Newsom"], ", ", ["a", {"href": "https://pitchfork.com/artists/470-bright-eyes/", "isExternal": false}, "Bright Eyes"], ", or ", ["a", {"href": "https://pitchfork.com/artists/3141-okkervil-river/", "isExternal": false}, "Okkervil River"], ", who never let their prodigious literary intelligence get in the way of crafting something you might actually enjoy listening to."], ["p", "To (sort of) quote Brandon Flowers: He's human ", ["em", "and"], " rocker. The existential despair of \"Something Soon\" is crystallized in a blown-out chorus, while he uses a hypnotic keyboard line to make the haunting \"Maud, You're Gone\" a prom song for moody kids. A spectral choir comes through a radio at the start of \"Sunburned Shirts\" before breaking into a scratchy pop gem, like George Harrison on anti-depressants (\"I haven't looked at the sun for so long/ I forgot how much it hurt to\"). Toledo's voice is weary, and carries a shred of desperation\u2014he sounds like a third-generation cassette tape recording of ", ["a", {"href": "pitchfork.com/artists/7320-julian-casablancas/", "isExternal": false}, "Julian Casablancas"], " (who, otherwise, is his complete opposite as a frontman)."], ["native-ad", {"position": "sponsor-product", "shouldDisplayLabel": true}], ["p", "Earlier this month, I went to a Car Seat Headrest show held as part of the annual CMJ Music Marathon, where dozens of bands go to make their reputations. But Toledo began the set lying on the floor, with his microphone angled toward the ground, as the band launched into ", ["a", {"href": "https://carseatheadrest.bandcamp.com/track/the-ending-of-dramamine", "rel": "nofollow noopener", "attributes": {"data-offer-url": "https://carseatheadrest.bandcamp.com/track/the-ending-of-dramamine"}, "isExternal": true}, "\"The Ending of Dramamine\""], ", a 14-minute epic where he references ", ["a", {"href": "https://pitchfork.com/artists/2800-modest-mouse/", "isExternal": false}, "Modest Mouse"], " and sings about only thinking about himself. If you weren't standing right at the stage, you couldn't see him. The words flowed from the void, sung by someone so overwhelmed by the moment he would rather disappear. I couldn't absorb them all at once but what I remember is the crowd standing on their toes, edging their way forward, hoping to catch a glimpse. Then, he stood up."]]

label: Saddle Creek
body_html: ["div", ["p", "The high-tech was once handmade. From the 1950s through the 1970s, computers stored data in ceramic rings called cores. These cores were strung with wire by a single worker and formed a neat grid of power and memory. Electricity being sent to one core would induct the adjacent wires, the activation of one bit empowering its neighbors. As a data storage solution, it was effective: each core could retain its data even if it lost power. As a craft object, it was elegant, a loom of information partway woven. This interdependent system of lines intersecting tiny nodes of history was called a coincidental core memory matrix, eventually shortened to \u201ccore memory.\u201d Like so much language and culture, that phrase has drifted from the abstract to the physical, only to wind up as a metaphor that feels completely unrelated\u2014words that were once meant to describe an arcane bit of computer science history are now used to refer to having really liked something as a child. Like a scrap of data, the phrase holds its origins in deep storage, even as it\u2019s powered by the meaning inherent within it; despite the overwhelming power and influence of capitalism, things always drift back toward the human."], ["cm-unit"], ["p", ["em", "bitknot"], " plants another peg in the circuit board. On Feeble Little Horse\u2019s third album\u2014and first without founding member Ryan Walchonski\u2014the Pittsburgh trio uses production tricks left over from Sebastian Kinsler\u2019s time making beats and singer Lydia Slocum\u2019s voice to wind sharp critiques of big tech around crunchy indie rock. While they haven\u2019t lost the homespun charm that made 2023\u2019s ", ["a", {"href": "https://pitchfork.com/reviews/albums/feeble-little-horse-girl-with-fish/", "isExternal": false}, ["em", "Girl With Fish"]], " feel like a particularly twee take on ", ["a", {"href": "https://pitchfork.com/reviews/albums/7674-cats-of-the-wild-vol-2/", "isExternal": false}, "Swirlies"], "-esque slacker shoegaze, their command of their sound has increased dramatically. The songs on ", ["em", "bitknot"], " are heavier, uglier, and far more glitched out than those on their predecessor. They\u2019re also lovelier, more full of life, and more empathetic."], ["inline-newsletter"], ["p", "The components might be familiar\u2014guitars that sound like they\u2019re played through a busted Zenith TV at full volume, heavy acoustic strumming \u00e0 la \u201990s folk-grunge group Days of the New, Slocum\u2019s fading read-out of a voice\u2014but they\u2019re all pulled into slightly unusual shapes. It\u2019s just enough to catch you off guard; while you\u2019re trying to figure out why \u201cDior\u201d\u2019s main riff sounds like it\u2019s missing a couple of notes, Slocum\u2019s take on how capitalism puts us into competition with one another slides in almost unnoticed. Like the systems it challenges, ", ["em", "bitknot"], " tries to rewire how you think and feel."], ["native-ad", {"position": "in-content", "shouldDisplayLabel": true}], ["p", "The songs are largely built around grimy riffs whose smears of overdrive sometimes blot out Slocum\u2019s voice and make the record feel like a sonic cousin to ", ["a", {"href": "https://pitchfork.com/reviews/albums/11882-psychocandy-darklands-automatic-honeys-dead-stoned-dethroned/", "isExternal": false}, ["em", "Psychocandy"]], ", so it feels weird to insist that this is music you need to hear in good headphones. And while there\u2019s always sunken treasures hiding in shoegaze\u2019s murky waters, so much of the sonic detail on ", ["em", "bitknot"], " bolsters the writing, upping the emotional impact of the songs. After a guitar punchout opens the record in the first seconds of \u201cDoorway,\u201d the band settles into a homemade ", ["a", {"href": "https://pitchfork.com/artists/3945-stereolab/", "isExternal": false}, "Stereolab"], " groove, while a distant guitar that sounds like a calliope pumps along. \u201cParis\u201d seems to emerge from the fallout of \u201cDior,\u201d its beatific vision of family vacation turned hyperreal and mildly horrifying by the way processed windchimes and field recordings of passing cars make it twinkle in the sun. Even the individual guitar tones feel set to the narrative tenor of the songs; the circle of distorted harmonics that ping through the dire \u201cDMT\u201d (\u201cdeath, money, tech\u201d) spin like a rusting can opener through tin, as if they\u2019re mimicking the way the internet rips us apart to harvest the meat within."], ["ad", {"position": "mid-content"}], ["p", "Slocum\u2019s voice is thin and soft, like the paper covering your doctor\u2019s examination table. Its translucence tends to catch the light the band shines through it: She\u2019s warm and glowing in the lazy afternoon haze of \u201cCradle,\u201d then one color among many in the rush of \u201cShopping.\u201d She sometimes seems to stumble into nostalgia in the middle of a line without ever indulging it, like when you\u2019re telling a story and remember a particularly fun detail but know you can\u2019t let it bog down the momentum. \u201cDoes this thing take diesel gasoline?/My country is what I need to leave,\u201d she sings in \u201cCradle\u201d with an everyday nonchalance. It feels like the right approach: The need to escape American life right now can be both urgent and kinda boring to talk about."], ["native-ad", {"position": "sponsor-product", "shouldDisplayLabel": true}], ["p", "It\u2019s generally boring to listen to other people sing about it, too, no matter how well-produced their record might be. And, to be sure, the last thing the world needs is another group of angsty indie rockers with too many unread Verso books on their shelves. What makes ", ["em", "bitknot"], "\u2019s critique work\u2014what makes it feel less like critique and closer to something like storytelling\u2014is in the way these songs understand that the evils of \u201clate\u201d capitalism aren\u2019t abstract concepts but the effects those concepts have on the lives of people subject to them. Meaning: It sucks to have your passions inflamed and your sense of self fractured because you\u2019re jealous of your hot friend\u2019s social feed. And it\u2019s humiliating to realize the whole thing has been engineered mostly to make Mark Zuckerberg richer."], ["p", "Petty jealousies ping across ", ["em", "bitknot"], ". \u201cShe\u2019s just like me but prettier/It\u2019s just not fair,\u201d Slocum sings in \u201cShopping\u201d before fantasizing about stealing the pretty girl\u2019s phone to rifle through her Ssense. In \u201cDior,\u201d she sends a kiss-off to some indie-rock frontperson: \u201cYou are not David Berman/You are not Kurt Cobain.\u201d The identity of the singer isn\u2019t the point\u2014their name is in fact bleeped out, like a curse on the radio\u2014so much as Slocum\u2019s frustration with having been forced into artistic battle by the need to sell records, and the way that battle makes people present as something bigger than what they actually are. She turns her knives inward, too. \u201cI\u2019m not insured/But nothing hurts/Wearing Ben Doctor,\u201d she sings, referencing the indie designer. It\u2019s an acknowledgment that the vanity and consumption the system instills in us is a way of bypassing the misery it creates; it\u2019s also a sincere celebration of looking and feeling good. She can\u2019t see a doctor, but she can be seen in one."], ["p", "Pleasure and pressure, individual desire and collective manipulation\u2014these would-be poles all overlap on ", ["em", "bitknot"], " because they can\u2019t be pried apart in life. This is an album in which harsh, scraping sounds make sweet vocal melodies sound even sweeter, where that kindness of spirit may flicker but never quite fades away. Far from a dogmatic takedown of our techno-capitalist ruling bros, ", ["em", "bitknot"], " is an empathetic, expertly arranged collection of songs that doesn\u2019t look down its nose at those of us struggling to feel good and create a little beauty inside of a system designed to make us miserable. For Feeble Little Horse, opting out of commerce and its millions of downstream effects isn\u2019t as simple as saying, \u201cI don\u2019t like that, and I won\u2019t be doing it.\u201d After all, we don\u2019t blame the target for being shot."]]

label: Dead Oceans
body_html: ["div", ["p", "How much feeling can fit inside a ", ["a", {"href": "https://pitchfork.com/artists/greg-mendez/", "isExternal": false}, "Greg Mendez"], " song? On \u201cFrog,\u201d from his new album, ", ["em", "Beauty Land"], ", he shows us. Here is every word he sings in it: \u201cPlease forgive me for my faults.\u201d His voice never rises above a hum. It\u2019s over in 73 seconds, but I haven\u2019t felt so harrowed by 73 consecutive seconds of music all year."], ["p", "How much life and detail can fit inside a Greg Mendez song? \u201cI pretend your garden\u2019s full of flowers every morning/They forgive me for the things I\u2019ve done and the things I will become when I\u2019m angry,\u201d he begins on \u201cSunsick\u201d\u2014within the space of one breath, he\u2019s situated us in a haunted landscape, a house, while Mendez unpacks the groceries, looks around, and realizes there is \u201cno one else I have to blame\u201d for this massive, human-sized loss. He sits alone, absorbing the hammer blow of his guilt and his total alienation within it. (That one maxes out the clock at 145 seconds.)"], ["cm-unit"], ["p", "Mendez has been writing these types of songs\u2014so plainspoken and open-hearted you fear for their safety\u2014for over 15 years now. ", ["em", "Beauty Land"], " is his debut since signing to Dead Oceans, but Mendez has altered nothing about his approach nor availed himself of any new resources to make it, because his music requires nothing he doesn\u2019t already have. He records everything alone, as he always has, and his songs cast their frightened shadows against your mind\u2019s eye, scurrying away into the deeper folds of your subconscious when you turn to look at them."], ["native-ad", {"position": "in-content", "shouldDisplayLabel": true}], ["p", "Maybe the room in West Philadelphia he recorded ", ["em", "Beauty Land"], " has better acoustics than your average bedroom, or maybe he just fussed a little longer with his set-up, but ", ["em", "Beauty"], " ", ["em", "Land"], " sounds just a ", ["em", "bit"], " sharper than Mendez\u2019s usual. The toy piano plinks on \u201cI Wanna Feel Pretty\u201d and \u201cNo Evil\u201d ring out with a steeliness that gives ", ["em", "Beauty Land"], " a starker profile than his previous records, as if there were late afternoon shadows framing every rough-handed strum and blot of keyboards. The difference is subtle, but it\u2019s unmistakable."], ["inline-newsletter"], ["p", "It\u2019s just as unmistakable who that profile reminds us of, and it\u2019s probably Mendez\u2019s curse that he can\u2019t weather a single review without someone invoking the name of ", ["a", {"href": "https://pitchfork.com/artists/3840-elliott-smith/", "isExternal": false}, "Elliott Smith"], ". And yet, he seems to be leaning into the spiritual link on ", ["em", "Beauty Land"], ", even encouraging it. Mendez\u2019s guitar has never so closely resembled the feathery Le Domino guitar that Smith immortalized on his early Kill Rock Stars albums, and there are moments when the sonic resemblance grows so startling that it prompts a ", ["em", "hey-wait-a-minute"], ". I had a ", ["em", "hey-wait-a-minute"], " happen to me at the outset of \u201cGentle Love,\u201d another on \u201cLooking Out Your Window,\u201d both of which not only replicate the sound of ", ["a", {"href": "https://pitchfork.com/reviews/albums/22947-eitheror-expanded-edition/", "isExternal": false}, ["em", "Either/Or"]], " and ", ["a", {"href": "https://pitchfork.com/reviews/albums/elliott-smith-elliott-smith/", "isExternal": false}, ["em", "Elliott Smith"]], " but seemingly bottle its air."], ["native-ad", {"position": "sponsor-product", "shouldDisplayLabel": true}], ["p", "Although Mendez might live inside the world Smith created, he sees his environs differently. Smith\u2019s songs often radiated cold anger at the \u201cyou\u2019s\u201d he sang to, while Mendez\u2019s songs are full of \u201cyou\u2019s\u201d who he can\u2019t help identifying with. \u201cYou\u2019re sincerely upset, so I ask what you want/But the late night stores don\u2019t keep it stocked,\u201d he sang on 2023\u2019s \u201c", ["a", {"href": "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ODaKPR35Tvs", "isExternal": false}, "Cop Caller"], ",\u201d with the empathy of someone who has navigated broken nervous systems his whole life, his own and others\u2019. It\u2019s a role he plays a few different times on ", ["em", "Beauty Land"], ", notably on \u201cConcussion,\u201d where he ruminates miserably on \u201ckicking a bad friend out.\u201d It seemed like the right thing to do, and yet why does he feel so awful about it?"], ["ad", {"position": "mid-content"}], ["p", "As he has for years, Mendez maps the dips and crags of addiction so plainly that to comment on his lyrics feels like standing in their way. On \u201cI Wanna Feel Pretty,\u201d he spends New Year\u2019s Eve alone, depressed and drinking \u201c\u2019til I couldn\u2019t remember my name.\u201d He checks himself into rehab, and then (seemingly) escapes, flush with an exhilaration that is only punctured by \u201cthe gleam in my eye where I see/The places I would be if I wasn\u2019t me.\u201d Read that line again, and ask yourself\u2014where does Mendez bury the tripwire? Where, exactly, does his gasp of freedom double back on itself, turn into a sob of despair?"], ["p", "You can\u2019t really, because Mendez\u2019s craft is so light that it disappears, absorbs itself into the bones of the music. \u201cGeranium,\u201d a late highlight on an album that could level you within half a lunch break, gave me difficulty breathing the first time I heard it. One of Mendez\u2019s friends exits the clinic only to start \u201cusing\u201d again. The friend calls Mendez, making up stories about fights, a broken nose. They break down crying on the phone. They swear they\u2019re trying; they really need that 20 bucks. Mendez holds the line. He repeats to the friend he loves them. The friend rebuffs him. The song ends on a pledge as provisional as it is devotional: \u201cI wouldn\u2019t hang up/I couldn\u2019t.\u201d Mendez\u2019s singing glows with the heat of someone who understands just how small they are\u2014the promises you need to make to keep living."], ["inline-embed", {"props": {"ctaHref": "https://cna.", "dangerousDek": "", "productBrand": "", "dangerousHed": "Greg Mendez: Beauty
